grh_dcd47dfe8c581352f851.title: The Coward
paragraphs: Britt discovers that a man wanted in Texas for his old life as a gun-toting bank robber has become a quiet rancher and promised his wife never to use a gun again. A neighboring rancher named Temple tries to force them off their land by sabotaging fences, killing cattle, and mocking Will as a coward. Will finally goes after Temple with a rifle but cannot break his promise and pull the trigger; instead he defeats Temple in a brutal fistfight. Seeing how completely the former outlaw has changed, Britt decides the law looking for a gunman has little reason to be interested in the rancher Will has become.

grh_dc8160d53d5c8ec9d6b9.title: Martha
paragraphs: Lady Harriet disguises herself as a servant named Martha for a visit to Richmond Fair and discovers too late that the joke has legally bound her to work for farmer Lionel. Lionel falls sincerely in love with Martha, while Harriet eventually flees and returns to her aristocratic life. When Lionel later recognizes Lady Harriet as the servant who deceived him, he feels betrayed. Harriet recreates the Richmond Fair at her castle to show him that the woman he loved still exists beneath the title, and Lionel chooses Harriet and Martha as 'two brides in one.'

grh_dc8dfefeeb38d77739eb.title: The Perfect Marriage
paragraphs: On their fifth anniversary, successful husband and wife Dale and Jenny Williams realize that their supposedly perfect marriage has gone flat and that familiarity has replaced romance. Talk of separation becomes serious when old flames Gloria and Gil reappear, giving each spouse reason to suspect the other has already moved on. The jealousy they thought had vanished returns with force, and both discover that they still care far more than they admitted. After comic attempts to provoke one another collapse, Dale and Jenny shut out their would-be alternatives, celebrate their anniversary after all, and rediscover the marriage they nearly abandoned.

grh_dc54ff767ea5b2d0d7f8.title: The Great March
paragraphs: A young woman joins a committee trying to stop an American fascist group from marching through town and becomes close to Jan, an older married man whose memories of fascism and wartime camps make the issue deeply personal. When the courts establish that the march is protected by the First Amendment, the committee searches for a response that will oppose the group without denying the same freedom it claims to defend. They decide the strongest protest is to ignore the march. The woman also ends her relationship with Jan rather than injure his wife and daughter, while Jan resolves to carry the renewed joy he found with her back into his family life.
